items: Scrollbars now match the app: thin, square and aqua instead of Windows' grey ones.
Fortnite installed with Epic's launcher can now be added, with the parts Epic installed (Save the World and LEGO Fortnite come along). Fishy Client reads which parts you have from the files on disk.
Updating Fortnite in Fishy Client downloads only the parts you have, plus any brand-new part. Epic's launcher keeps working too; updating in one may make the other update again.
Games with optional parts that aren't installed yet are installed with Epic's launcher first: Fishy Client then adds them by itself.
Downloads can be faster: each download first tries all of Epic's download servers for a moment and uses the fastest. If a server fails, the next one takes over.
When a download speed limit is on, the Downloads page says so ("Limited to 1 MB/s") with a link to change it in Settings.

You can install games into Epic's own folder (C:\Program Files\Epic Games): press Use Epic's folder in the Install box or in Settings. Windows asks for permission once per game, the same way Epic's launcher does.

Games another store installs, such as STAR WARS Battlefront II through the EA app, now show in your Library with "Installs through the EA app" instead of under Not on Windows. Fishy Client can't install or start those: use Epic's launcher or the EA app.
Games you haven't installed look a bit greyer in the Library, so your installed ones stand out more.
Games you already installed with Epic's launcher can be added without downloading them again: press Add them at the top of the Library.
If some of their files are missing or damaged, Download them fetches only those.
Fishy Client can now update itself: when a new version is out, a bar offers Update now (you can turn the check off in Settings).
The ⋯ menu of an installed game shows how much space it takes.
The Install box warns about folders that need administrator rights, such as C:\Program Files\Epic Games.
Games you haven't installed look a bit grey in the Library.
The Install box says that Epic's launcher can't see games installed with Fishy Client.
This What's new box.
The first version: sign in with Epic, see your Library, install, play and update your games.
Pause and resume downloads, with a speed limit if you want one.
Library filters and sorting, and a Running badge while a game is open.
Settings, logs without secrets, and Delete all my data.
A Windows installer (.msi).
